title: Non-Acted Text and Keystrokes Database and Learning Methods to Recognize Emotions

experimental_conditions.environment: General-purpose computing laboratory with audio and video facilities
experimental_conditions.baseline_condition: Participants faced a wall for one minute
experimental_conditions.writing_task: Participants wrote reviews in an unguided manner

data_split.validation: 20 different combinations of training and validation data were evaluated

proposed_method.name: Hybrid text + keystroke features with Mutual Information (MI Gain) feature selection and Discriminant Analysis
proposed_method.description: A hybrid approach combining text and keystroke features, with Mutual Information feature selection followed by a Discriminant Analysis classifier

primary_performance.experimental_condition: Five-class classification of basic human emotions on the DEKT-345 × 2 dataset

third_evaluation_field.value: Sum, mean, and standard deviation of time duration of each letter (a to z)

evidence.statement: Obtained results showed that the sum, mean, and standard deviation values of time duration of keys have high scores than others, while the frequency of space key and backspace key (rate of error) have scored higher than remaining frequency-based features, however, they score lesser than sum, mean, and keys' time standard deviation.

dataset.statement: Experiments are conducted on DEKT-345 x 2 dataset, which consists of 345 text samples and 345 keystrokes samples of the five basic human emotions (total of 690 samples).

primary_performance.section: 5.1 Results on DEKT-345 x 2 Dataset for Five Class Problem
primary_performance.statement: MI technique and discriminant analysis had 86.95% accuracy on the hybrid data.
